title: India Lets Wealth-Focused Funds With $463 Billion Invest Abroad
summary: India’s market regulator will allow a $463 billion segment of its portfolio management industry — funds catering to wealthy individuals — to invest in overseas securities and undertake short selling in equity options for the first time as part of a massive overhaul of rules.

title: Bond Losses Build on Inflation, Rate-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
summary: A global bond selloff extended into Asia as elevated oil prices stoked inflation concerns, pushing long-term Treasury yields to multi-decade highs and fueling expectations for further interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

title: AI Boom Can Withstand Higher Rates: Goldman's Moe

title: Kobayashi in $3.2 Billion Buyout Talks After Red-Yeast Case

title: Lula to Ban Online Betting, Offer Debt Relief Before Election

title: Global Citizen CEO on Mission To End Extreme Poverty
summary: Global Citizen CEO Hugh Evans sat down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to discuss the organization's upcoming Global Citizen Festival in New York City, the mission to end extreme poverty, and more. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Does Iced Coffee Pass the Vibe Check?
summary: The very nature of work is in flux right now, with artificial intelligence accelerating the deepening structural shifts. Employers and their young employees are caught in a power struggle over who gets to decide the norms of this new workplace. Iced coffee is just the latest proxy for that tension — how each party feels both misunderstood and deep anxiety about their place in this evolving landscape, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Beth Kowitt says. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Savor CEO on Producing Fats & Oils From Carbon Sources
summary: Savor CEO Kathleen Alexander explains how the company builds fats and oils molecule by molecule from carbon-based inputs, aiming to reduce reliance on traditional agriculture while matching the taste and functionality of conventional fats. She discusses Savor’s pilot production, commercial partnerships, and why the company sees supply-chain resilience and sustainability as major opportunities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: CFOs Face a Tougher Call on When to Borrow
summary: It’s been a good year for CFOs looking to borrow. Credit markets have largely remained open despite the war in Iran, spreads have been low and investors have been eager to buy. Mozilla CFO Eric Muhlheim and Bloomberg's Nina Trentmann discuss the impact of AI on capex spend, corporate strategy, and company principles in our CFO Briefing. They speak with Bloomberg Businessweek Daily hosts Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chicago Schools Shed 11,500 Students as Risk of Budget Cuts Grow

title: NATO's Rutte: Putin 'Not Playing Ball' in Ukraine Peace Talks
summary:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said Russian President Vladimir Putin is ‘not playing ball’ when it comes to progress on Ukraine peace talks. He also argued that Europeans are ‘prepared’ for Russian hybrid attacks.
 Rutte spoke with Bloomberg’s Annmarie Hordern on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)
